directAnswer:
The size of the generated file is not the cause. Chrome parses the sheet in 5 to 13 ms (measured by the earlier lanes).

The CSS work is the cause. With an empty sheet, a page needs 42% to 71% less main thread time (measured by the earlier lanes). This lane found the work in three places of the primitive layer:
1. The formulas of the layer utilities of @ariakit/tailwind cost 57 µs for each element of a full recalculation.
2. The hover glider of a nav makes one arrow key recalculate the whole list: 1,245 of 1,734 elements.
3. Two rule shapes make Chrome recalculate a whole subtree: a `:has()` shape (10 class names) and a sibling shape (3 class names).

The lab did two things without need:
- Live frames in the gallery: about 94% of its wait.
- Four gliders on the screenshot list. The note of the maintainer asked for the bar glider. The bar glider alone costs 87 elements and 48 ms for one arrow key, not 96 ms.

The real app will not be slow as the lab is. It is one document, and its list has the bar glider only (apps/web/src/review/item-list.tsx:307). But its copy of the primitives has the same 3 class names of the sibling shape. So each tooltip, menu, or dialog that mounts can recalculate the document. That is counted from code, not measured in apps/web.

Before the settled design goes into apps/web:
- One prop of the list removes its largest cost.
- Two tested rewrites in Ariakit UI remove two more costs.
- The cost of the formulas stays.

fullDocumentInvalidation:
Found. The cause has two parts, and each is necessary.

**1. The trigger (lab design code).** `apps/lab/src/explorations/kits/ariakit/variants/pager.tsx:61` gives each mark of the variant control the key of its variant:

```tsx
<Hint key={variant.key} label={...}>
```

A new screenshot removes each `Hint` and adds a new one. Each Ariakit tooltip has a portal node that is a child of `<body>`. With each folder open, one ArrowDown removes 3 `div#portal/...` from `<body>` and adds 3 (results/B-body-children-all.log). At 41 rows no child of the body changes, which is why the cost showed only with the folders open. The stack of the invalidation is the cleanup of `usePortal` (`t.remove()`).

**2. The rules (Ariakit UI style layer).** DevTools names one invalidation set with `allDescendantsMightBeInvalid` on `BODY`, with three selectors (results/B-body-selectors.txt):
- `styles/glider.ts:129`: `not-peer-ui-focus-visible:outline-none`
- `styles/glider.ts:138`: `not-ui-sibling-selected:hidden`
- `styles/tabs.ts:381`: `not-peer-ui-focus-visible:invisible`

They come from two custom variants: `ui-focus-visible` (`styles/ui.css:1063`) and `ui-sibling-selected` (`styles/ui.css:1256`). Tailwind writes `~ *` for `peer-*` and for `not-` on a sibling variant:

```css
.not-peer-ui-focus-visible\:outline-none:not(:is(:where(.peer):is(:focus-visible, [data-focus-visible]) ~ *))
```

**Bisection** (CSSOM, 585 rows, size containers off, load 5; results/B1-three-rules.log):
- Sheet as built: 2,477 elements for each key.
- One of the three rules removed: 2,475 to 2,477.
- The three removed: 138. Style and layout: 282 ms against 87 ms.

**The exact shape** (26 rules that match no element, added one at a time; results/B2, B3, B4-synthetic.log):
- Slow: a sibling combinator (`~` or `+`) with `*` at its right, where an alternative at its left has no class, id, or attribute. Examples: `:focus-visible ~ *`, `:is(:focus-visible, [data-x]) ~ *`, `:is(:checked, [aria-x]) ~ *`, `input:checked ~ *`. Also at the top level, and with `:where(.q)` beside the `:is()` list.
- Fast: each alternative at the left has a class or an attribute (`:where(.q):focus-visible ~ *`, `:is(.q:checked, [a]) ~ *`); or a class at the right (`:is(:checked, [a]) ~ .z`); or `:has(~ ...)`.

With the slow shape in the sheet, each insertion or removal of an element makes Chrome recalculate the subtree of the parent of that element. A child of `<body>` gives the document.

**Smallest change, tested** (patch.py `fixsib`, copy lab-fixsib):

```css
/* styles/ui.css:1063. As built: &:is(:focus-visible, [data-focus-visible]) */
@custom-variant ui-focus-visible {
  &:focus-visible,
  &[data-focus-visible] { @slot; }
}
/* styles/ui.css:1256, ui-sibling-selected: the list at the left of ~ starts with */
:is(:checked:where(.control), [aria-checked="true"], ...) ~ &,
```

- Result with the bar glider: 2,480 elements become 129 (rules removed: 127).
- Result with four gliders and the hover rewrite: 2,485 become 133, and 342 ms becomes 139 ms.
- Pictures: 0 pixels differ in 6 states of both views.
- The sheet grows from 429,987 to 436,633 bytes.

App-side change: `<Hint key={index}>` gives 45 elements. It fails when the number of variants changes (338 ms).

**Second exact result (the cause of the 41-row cost).** The hover glider of a nav, `styles/nav.ts:381` and `:385`, has `.nav:not(:has(...)) > &`. That makes the nav a `:has()` anchor outside the subject. With the `:has()` rule shape in the sheet, each change inside the nav recalculates the nav. Glider subsets as builds, largest recalculation of one key:
- hover + bar: 1,215
- selected + bar: 69
- focus + bar: 69
- selected + focus + bar: 70

Tested rewrite (patch.py `fixhover`):

```ts
"[.nav:hover>&:not(:has(~.control:hover,~*_li>.control:hover))]:delay-250",
"[&:not(:has(~.control:hover,~*_li>.control:hover))]:hidden",
```

Four gliders with it: largest recalculation 71, not 1,217; next frame 35 ms, not 82 ms.

The mechanism inside Chrome (one shared invalidation set) is an inference from the DevTools events and these experiments. The source of Chrome was not read.
typedProperties:
No faster form with an equal picture was found. The typed rules are not the cost. They limit it.

Method: one loaded review page (1,610 to 1,734 elements). For each variant, the changed `@property` rules go into the page. Then 4 theme switches (each is a full recalculation), size containers off, 5 rounds in turns, load 70 to 77. The pictures are from a page load with the changed sheet. Results: results/C-recalc-large.log, C-recalc-inherit.log, C-recalc-single.log, C-pictures-load.log, C-layer-strip-large.log.

The 51 typed rules of `node_modules/@ariakit/tailwind/src/output.css` (lines 1547 to 2251) are 14 `<color>`, 26 `<number>`, and 11 `<length>`; 32 have `inherits: false`.

Full sheet: 57.2 µs for each element [56.3-61.1], 92 ms for one recalculation.

| Variant | µs for each element | Against the full sheet | Pixels that differ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| The 51 removed | 17.9 | 69% less | 83% (broken) |
| 10 layer colors removed | 705 | 12 times more | 2.5% |
| 8 text and ink rules removed | 56.9 | 1% less | 0.26% |
| 18 frame rules removed | 56.3 | 2% less | 59% |
| 15 other numbers removed | 28.9 | 49% less | 83% (broken) |
| 32 with `inherits: false` removed | 34.9 | 39% less | 84% |
| 19 with `inherits: true` removed | 275 | 4.8 times more | 82% |

Is the cost the registration, `inherits: false`, or the formulas?
- Not the type. The same rules with `syntax: "*"` (same `inherits` and `initial-value`): the 14 colors are 14 times slower (2.8% of pixels differ); the 11 lengths are 6.7 times slower (0.46%); the 51 are 22 times slower. The 26 numbers give an equal picture (0 pixels) and 8% to 11% more time.
- Not `inherits: false`. The 32 rules with `inherits: true` and the same type: 7% more time.
- Single rules: no single removal is outside the range of the full sheet on the fast side (that run had 56 to 121 µs, load 40 to 90). Two are far on the slow side: without `--ak-frame-radius` 493 µs, without `--ak-layer` 131 µs.
- One more real alternative: the classes `ak-layer ak-layer-transparent` removed from the 304 of 523 layer elements that have no other layer, state, or edge class. Result: 10% less (89.6 to 80.7 ms), but 2.9% (dark) and 4.7% (light) of the pixels differ.

Reading: the time goes away only where a removal breaks the formulas that `ak-layer` writes (`output.css:118-162`: a chain of 7 relative colors and 4 more from `--ak-layer`), and then the page is broken. The earlier "56% to 58% upper limit" cannot be reached by a change of the registrations. Which formula costs how much was not measured: a formula cannot be removed alone with an equal picture.

The times are of a full recalculation after a theme switch, not of a page load. The page-load form was stopped, because one load with the CPU slowed 4 times needed about one minute at a load of 100 to 220.

proposedDecisions.question: Which gliders does the screenshot list of the review page have?
proposedDecisions.options: (a) four-as-built: keep the four gliders. 96 ms, 438 to 515 ms at 4x, pointer 429 ms, wheel 879 ms. (b) bar-only: 48 ms, 188 to 276 ms at 4x, 87 elements; equal picture at 41 rows; only the bar travels; in a folder the focus ring is 3 px inside the row. (c) all-but-hover: selected, focus, and bar gliders. 49 ms, 200 ms at 4x, 97 elements; pictures equal in both views; the hover surface does not travel. (d) row-draws-bar: 41 ms, 79 elements; in a folder the bar does not show; hand-placed code. (e) four-after-ariakit: four gliders after the rewrite in Ariakit UI. 49 ms, 204 ms at 4x, 97 elements; pointer 236 ms and wheel 306 ms stay; waits for another repository.
proposedDecisions.recommended: bar-only. It is the form of the note of lab round 1 and of apps/web/src/review/item-list.tsx:307. It needs one prop and no primitive change. It is the simplest form, with 87 recalculated elements, not 1,245.
proposedDecisions.wrongIf: The maintainer wants the selected surface or the focus ring to travel between rows: then all-but-hover has the same speed for the keys. Or Safari or Firefox behave in another way: only Chrome was measured.

proposedDecisions.question: What must be true for the speed of the review page before the settled design goes into apps/web, and who acts first?
proposedDecisions.options: (a) count-gate-app-first: a browser test fails when an arrow key or Approve recalculates more than 300 elements (today 1,245 and 2,614 as built; 87 and 223 with the bar glider only; 45 with each folder open when the tooltips stay). The app acts first (the glider choice, and marks that keep their tooltips); the Ariakit rewrites follow with the next refresh of the copy. (b) time-gate: each main key below 200 ms with the CPU slowed 4 times. The best stock form was at the line in three sessions: 276, 188, 198 ms for the arrow key and 305, 225, 230 ms for Approve; it needs a quiet machine and less script. (c) ariakit-first: the three rewrites go into Ariakit UI first, then the copy is refreshed (D-UI-02), then the design goes in with four gliders. Rewrite 2 has no tested form. (d) no-gate: merge as built (438 to 515 ms and 480 to 555 ms at 4x).
proposedDecisions.recommended: count-gate-app-first. A count is the same on a quiet and on a busy machine, so the gate is stable in CI. The app can remove the largest cost today with no change of the primitives.
proposedDecisions.wrongIf: A measurement on a quiet machine shows more than 200 ms for a main key with the CPU slowed 4 times after the app changes. Then the count gate is not enough, and script time needs its own limit (style and layout were 88 ms of 276 ms).

proposedDecisions.question: Does the gallery of the lab show pictures in place of live frames?
proposedDecisions.options: (a) keep-live-frames: no work; the gallery is usable after 9 to 19 s in development and 4 to 10 s in the production form; one saved file blocks the main thread for 2.3 to 5.5 s. (b) pictures: pictures in the gallery and the directions page, live frames in the two explorers; usable after about 1 s in development and 0.5 s in the production form; a card no longer follows the theme and look controls.
proposedDecisions.recommended: pictures. The frames are about 94% of the wait of the gallery (measured by the earlier lanes).
proposedDecisions.wrongIf: The maintainer no longer opens the gallery. The design is settled and the lab is temporary, so no work is then the simpler choice.

limits:
- No time is the time of a quiet machine. The load average was 4 to 223 on 14 cores. Forms ran in turns, 5 runs each. The counts are stable; read the times as ratios. The 200 ms line with the CPU slowed 4 times is not settled: the bar form had 276, 188, and 198 ms in three sessions.
